segment.description: Big Rock Creek, Marshall County, Tennessee (catalog) — a small Duck River tributary through Lewisburg, rising in southwest Marshall County and flowing north about 20 river miles to its confluence with the Duck River (TDEC's nearest mainstem station is described as 'HIGHWAY 272 DOWNSTEAM BIG ROCK CREEK' at 35.577, -86.779, HUC 06040002). Catalog YAML carries no counties field; identity resolved from the catalog hydroIdentity (GNIS 01305230, HUC8 06040002) and confirmed against WQP station metadata: every 'Big Rock Creek' station found sits in HUC 06040002 with county code 117 (Marshall), matching the catalog note 'TWRA winter-stocked Marshall County creek near Lewisburg'. Same-named Big Rock Creeks elsewhere in Tennessee were not an issue here — all stations returned by the Marshall County sweep belong to this creek.
segment.boundaries: The named Big Rock Creek within Marshall County (HUC 06040002); identity stations USGS-03599000 'BIG ROCK CREEK AT LEWISBURG, TN' (24.9 sq mi, alt 705.01 ft NGVD29) and USGS-03599100 'BIG ROCK CR AT DOUBLE BRIDGES, TN' (48.7 sq mi, alt 644.37 ft). TWRA's stocking-site string is 'Big Rock Greenway' (Region 2, Marshall) with no reach detail; the greenway lies along the creek in Lewisburg, so in-town gauge USGS-03599000 is the nearest temperature station to the stocking site.

coldSource.notes: Elevation 705.01 ft is the USGS-03599000 station altitude at Lewisburg (NGVD29); the downstream Double Bridges station sits at 644.37 ft — a low-relief agricultural/urban Marshall County valley with no gorge or canopy documentation found. No cold-water source of any kind documented. TDEC station TDECWPC-BROCK006.0ML is described as '100 YARDS DOWNSTREAM DAM AT VERONA', evidencing an unnamed small dam on the creek at Verona; no operator or release documentation exists, and the 26.3 deg C July 2000 grab below it shows no cold-release effect. Identity verified from WQP station metadata columns (station names, Marshall County code 117, HUC 06040002) because the USGS identity endpoint has been 503ing this week.

holdover.detail: No holdover documentation found. The TWRA program is winter-only catchable rainbows at 'Big Rock Greenway': 2026 workbook rows (Region 2, Marshall, type Winter, Rainbow Trout) are 1/15/2026, 2/27/2026 and TBD 12/2026; the live TWRA stocking page contains the 'Big Rock Greenway' site string (fetched copy's flattened table interleaves two tables, so its stray date cells cannot be attributed). No source documents survival between stockings or through summer, and the in-town summer record (USGS-03599000 nearest the greenway: 24.7-32.0 deg C June-September grabs) makes summer survival implausible on the cited temperatures alone.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documentation found in any agency source for Big Rock Creek. TWRA's Trout Management Plan 2017-2027 places Tennessee's wild trout in East Tennessee and describes hatchery-supported streams and lakes as 'primarily warmwater habitats that cannot support trout year round' (canon quote; PDF not fetched per rule).

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: 91 June-September grab samples across 1966-2025 on every reach of Big Rock Creek run 18.5-32.0 deg C — 25.3-32.0 deg C at the in-town Lewisburg gauge nearest the Big Rock Greenway stocking site — far above year-round trout survival thresholds.

segment.description: Boiling Fork Creek, a small Franklin County stream in the Sewanee/Cowan area draining to the Elk River system (GNIS 01269369, HUC 06030003). TWRA winter put-and-take rainbow trout water, stocked at Cowan City Park (Franklin County).

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout presence documented; the creek is outside TWRA's wild trout waters and sits in a warmwater Elk River drainage.

segment.description: Buffalo River main stem (GNIS 01295866 / 01305509, HUC-8 06040004), the longest un-impounded river in Middle Tennessee and longest tributary of the Duck River, flowing north ~125+ miles from Lawrence County through Lewis, Wayne, Perry, and Humphreys counties to its Duck River confluence - NOT the Little Buffalo River (separate catalog water) and NOT Buffalo Creek (Grainger). Temperature record cited here is USGS 03604000 'BUFFALO RIVER NEAR FLAT WOODS, TN' (Perry County), the catalog's gauge; TDEC also maintains BUFFA017.7PE and USGS has 03604400/03604500 at Lobelville on the lower river.
segment.boundaries: Catalog: 'north-flowing Duck River tributary through Lewis, Perry, and Humphreys counties' with USGS 03604000 as the reference gauge - i.e., the middle/lower agricultural and gorge reaches around Perry/Humphreys. TDEC's 2026 scenic designation covers 'The entire river' (~127.8 mi including the Lawrence/Wayne headwaters), a longer reach than the catalog notes name.

coldSource.notes: TDEC: 'The Buffalo River is the longest un-impounded river in middle Tennessee and the longest tributary of the Duck River' - there is no dam anywhere on the main stem, so no tailwater mechanism exists. The river meanders over 125 miles through the southern and western portions of Middle Tennessee supporting 'a diversity of wildlife including nearly 85 species of fish' (TDEC), and is a noted canoeing/kayaking stream with a TWRA access at Henryville. No spring influence and no cold-water mechanism is documented in any source checked; the Flat Woods gauge reads 24-27 C in summer.

holdover.detail: No trout presence of any kind is documented, so no holdover question arises. TWRA has never stocked the Buffalo River main stem: the 2026 row-level schedule contains zero 'Buffalo River' rows (only Little Buffalo River in Lawrence Co. and Buffalo Creek in Grainger Co., both different waters), and the catalog itself carries stockingProgram false.

segment.description: Center Hill Reservoir itself - the 18,220-acre USACE impoundment of the Caney Fork east of Smithville across DeKalb, Putnam, Warren, and White counties. Distinct from the celebrated trout tailwater below Center Hill Dam (cataloged as caney-fork-river) and from the free-flowing river above the lake (caney-fork-upper).
segment.boundaries: Full pool at Center Hill Dam (Caney Fork river-mile ~26) upstream through the Caney Fork, Collins, and Calfkiller arms; county spread DeKalb/Putnam/Warren/White per TWRA.

coldSource.notes: TWRA states 'The United States Army Corps of Engineers is the operating authority of Center Hill Reservoir' (18,220 acres; DeKalb, Putnam, Warren, White counties). The bottom-draw release (~120-ft-deep orifice gate, reinstalled June 2024) describes the dam's deep discharge - it is what makes the TAILWATER below the dam cold, not the lake itself: the reservoir is thermally stratified (Devlin & Bettoli 1999 documented the stratification driving the hypolimnial tailwater release), and the one WQP surface reading at the near-dam reservoir station was 31.63 C in July 2012. TWRA's lake fishery page lists black bass, crappie, walleye, bluegill, catfish - no trout.

holdover.detail: No trout are stocked into the lake (TWRA's 2026 stocking feed has zero Center Hill LAKE rows - the only 'Center Hill' row is 'Center Hill TW / Caney Fork River', the tailwater below the dam), so no lake holdover is documented either way.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documented. TWRA's reservoir page describes the fishery as black bass (largemouth/smallmouth/spotted), crappie, walleye, bluegill, catfish with detailed black-bass survey commentary and no trout mention. coldSource.notes: Full summer pool 875 ft MSL (winter pool 864 ft), per TVA lake information. A eutrophic tributary reservoir per the Tennessee 305(b) reporting cited by EPA NEPIS archives - warm, productive basin, not a cold deep-release storage reservoir in the South Holston/Watauga sense.

segment.description: Stones River MAIN STEM, Davidson County, Tennessee (catalog) — the Nashville-metro reach below J. Percy Priest Dam, anchored on the Donelson gauge. This is the below-dam tailwater reach where TWRA's winter rainbow program occurs; it is distinct from the East Fork (batch-2 record east-fork-stones-river) and the West Fork (its own catalog slug). Composite-trap check: TWRA's 2026 workbook tags the stocking site 'J. Percy Priest TW / Stones River' to Davidson County — the same county as this catalog entry — and NWS gauge JPPT1 'Stones River below J Percy Priest Dam' is also Davidson, so the stocked tailwater coincides with (at least the upper part of) this catalog reach. The dam itself sits on the Rutherford/Wilson/Davidson line; agency text does not distinguish stocking banks above or below the county line.
segment.boundaries: J. Percy Priest Dam downstream to the Cumberland River confluence (TWRA's regulation-exceptions reach: 'Stones River from its confluence with the Cumberland upstream to J. coldSource.notes: Elevation is the USGS gauge altitude at Donelson (382.36 ft NAVD88, waterservices site output). NWS gauge JPPT1 'Stones River below J Percy Priest Dam' carries data attribution to the US Army Corps of Engineers (Nashville District, lrn.usace.army.mil). TWRA manages this tailwater as a winter put-and-take, not a cold-release trout tailwater: TWRA's Cheatham Reservoir page says the tailwater's trout 'will not survive the warm summer water temperatures' — i.e., the agency itself documents that the below-dam releases do not keep this reach cold through summer. USGS identity verified via waterservices site service (the USGS identity endpoint has been 503ing this week); WQP returned zero discrete temperature samples for 03430200 (header-only CSV).

holdover.detail: TWRA explicitly documents the opposite of holdover on this reach: 'Trout are good to eat and will not survive the warm summer water temperatures. Anglers are encouraged to harvest...' The USGS continuous record at Donelson for July 2025 (n=2,974 readings) shows min 22.5, mean 25.0, max 28.2 deg C — consistent with TWRA's statement. The fishery is a Dec-Mar catchable rainbow put-and-take: Dale Hollow National Fish Hatchery stocks ~2,000 rainbows below the dam beginning the first Friday in December, with January and February events (2026 workbook rows: 1/9/2026, 02/13/2026, TBD 12/2026; TWRA table row 'J. Percy Priest Dam, Stones River — Rainbow — December through March').

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documentation for this reach. The fishery TWRA describes is entirely stocked put-and-take (Dale Hollow NFH catchable rainbows, winter only). TWRA's Trout Management Plan 2017-2027 places Tennessee's wild trout resources in East Tennessee streams and states that hatchery-supported waters are 'primarily warmwater habitats that cannot support trout year round' (plan not fetched per PDF ban; URL cited).

segment.description: Tims Ford Lake/Reservoir itself - the 10,600-acre Elk River impoundment near Winchester with a major portion in Franklin County (catalog: Franklin/Moore counties). This record deliberately does NOT transfer tailwater facts to the lake: the trout fishery and March-December stocking TWRA documents are for the Elk River BELOW Tims Ford Dam, which is the separate elk-river catalog entry (evidenced in the habitat-survival batch 1).
segment.boundaries: Catalog: reference waterbody from the Tennessee waterways inventory - the whole reservoir, Tims Ford Dam (completed 1970, TVA-owned/operated per TWRA's live page) upstream along the Elk River and its arms (including the Boiling Fork and Tims Ford Creek arms). Full pool 888 ft msl, winter pool 873 ft msl.

coldSource.notes: This water is the IMPOUNDMENT, not a tailwater - damTailwater is null for the lake itself. The impounding structure is Tims Ford Dam, completed 1970; TWRA's live reservoir page states 'The Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) owns and operates Tims Ford Reservoir' (note: the roster's working assumption of USACE operation is contradicted by TWRA's page - TVA-built and TVA-operated). Full pool elevation 888 ft msl (value above). The dam's deep cold releases support the documented Elk River tailwater trout stocking below the dam - a different catalog water; none of that program applies inside the lake.

holdover.detail: Not applicable as documented - TWRA stocks no trout in the reservoir at all (the TWRA stocking workbook and its official source table contain zero trout rows for Tims Ford Lake; the only 'Tims Ford' trout row is 'Tims Ford TW / Elk River', the tailwater below the dam), so there is no stocked cohort that could hold over. No agency holdover documentation exists for the lake.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild or resident trout documentation of any kind for the reservoir. TWRA's 'What you can catch' list and regulations for Tims Ford are entirely warmwater (black bass, crappie, catfish, striped/hybrid bass, white/yellow bass, walleye, sunfish); no trout entry appears anywhere on the page.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: Measured summer surface temperatures on the reservoir run 27.3-31.0 C (2002-2023), TWRA stocks trout only in the river below Tims Ford Dam and not in the lake, and the lake is absent from TWRA's 8-water year-round reservoir trout program.

segment.description: The upper (headwater) reach of Roan Creek in Johnson County, cold water near the Virginia line in the Roan Mountain drainage, TWRA-stocked as 'Upper Roan Creek'.
segment.boundaries: Catalog covers the upper creek; TWRA's stocking workbook rows are likewise labeled 'Upper Roan Creek' (Johnson County) without mile limits. REACH NOTE: the special trout regulation TWRA sets on Roan Creek - 'Mountain Lake Estates Bridge downstream to Doe Creek' (eregulations Region 4, 2026 live) - applies to the LOWER main stem, a different reach; it is not evidence for the upper creek.

coldSource.notes: Free-flowing mountain headwater creek (catalog: 'Cold Johnson County water near the Virginia line'); no dam or spring source claimed. Nearest gauge evidence is downstream: USGS-03482000 'ROAN CREEK NEAR NEVA, TN' (102 sq mi, below the headwater forks) grabbed 17.0 C on 1988-07-06, while the lower main stem at USGS-03482100 near Doeville (110 sq mi) ran 17.8-26.1 C in summer 1975-76 grabs - a headwater-to-valley warming gradient. No station exists on the stocked upper reach itself. TDEC station records carry '303D' tags on Roan Creek main-stem names (e.g. TDECWPC-ROAN011.6JO); the impairment cause was not verified in this pass. Station identities verified via WQP Station metadata (USGS identity endpoint down this week).

holdover.detail: No holdover documentation found. TWRA's 2026 stocking program for the water is weekly seasonal stockings (see troutSpecies) with no summer/winter continuity and no posted post-stocking persistence data.

wildPopulation.detail: Brook-trout wild candidacy is NOT borne out by the current official lists: Roan Creek (any reach) appears nowhere on the wild-trout-streams list on TWRA's regulations publisher page (wild list members in this corner of the state are Beaverdam Creek (Johnson Co), Laurel Fork and Left Prong Hampton Creek (Carter Co), Paint Creek and Rocky Fork (Greene/Unicoi), plus Monroe County waters). Another Johnson County wild water (Beaverdam Creek) is on the list, but that fact does not transfer to Roan Creek. No STMP or Cherokee NF document found in this pass documenting a wild trout population in the upper creek.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: The nearest gauge below the headwater forks grabbed 17.0 C in July 1988 in a Roan Mountain drainage where the upper reach lies above the valley warming (lower main stem hit 26.1 C), but stocking is spring-to-early-summer only and nothing documents trout persisting year-round.

segment.description: Watauga Lake (Watauga Reservoir), the 6,430-acre TVA impoundment of the Watauga River in the northeast Tennessee mountains (Carter County; formed 1948), with the pool running to Watauga Dam at its west end.
segment.boundaries: Entire reservoir pool behind Watauga Dam (TVA). Excludes the short Watauga River reach between Watauga Dam and Wilbur Lake (catalog watauga-river-wilbur-reach), Wilbur Reservoir, and the Wilbur Dam tailwater (catalog watauga-river) - all separate entries downstream.

damTailwater.dam: Watauga Dam (TVA, completed 1948) impounds the lake; its deep releases feed the downstream Wilbur chain

coldSource.notes: TWRA's Watauga Reservoir page (fetched live 2026-09-18) states lake trout were 'selected for stocking because of the cold, well-oxygenated, habitat present', that the best lake trout fishing is between Watauga Point and Butler Bridge, and directs summer anglers to troll spoons for lake trout 'in 90 to 120 feet of water' (rainbow/brown summer trolling at 30-50 ft) - a TWRA-documented cold, oxygenated deep layer through summer. Water levels fluctuate up to 44 ft between summer full pool and winter drawdown (same page). No verified surface-elevation figure was found on citable pages, so elevationFt is null. The deep-release character of the system is corroborated downstream: USGS-03483980 at Wilbur Dam (discharge of the Watauga-Dam-fed chain) measured 8.0-9.5 C in June-July and 10.0 C in mid-August 1976 (see the watauga-river-wilbur-reach record for that station's data).

holdover.detail: No agency holdover/creel study located for the reservoir. TWRA's statewide plan states stocking 'is required to maintain' these nine reservoir trout fisheries (Watauga among them), i.e. the fishery is maintained by stocking rather than claimed as self-sustaining; the summer lake-trout fishery itself implies multi-year residence of stocked fish but no citable holdover metric was found.

wildPopulation.detail: No natural trout reproduction documented in the reservoir; TWRA's plan states stocking is required to maintain the reservoir trout fishery.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: Watauga is named on TWRA's live reservoir trout stocking list - 'TWRA stocks the following reservoirs with trout to provide year-round trout fishing opportunities' ('Region IV, Watauga - Lake and Rainbow') - and TWRA's own page documents the cold, well-oxygenated deep habitat that lets it stock lake trout, a species requiring summer water far colder than any warmwater impoundment provides.

segment.description: The short (~1.5 mile) riverine Watauga River between Watauga Dam and Wilbur Lake (Wilbur Reservoir) in Carter County - the cold, clear release water closing the Watauga Lake -> Wilbur Lake -> Watauga River tailwater chain.
segment.boundaries: Watauga Dam (USGS 03483950 below-dam gauge; spillway-release station 03483600) downstream ~1.5 miles to the head of Wilbur Reservoir (Wilbur Dam sits ~3 river miles below Watauga Dam at Watauga River Mile 34 per TWRA's Wilbur Tailwater plan). SIBLING TRAP GUARD: this is NOT the celebrated Wilbur tailwater below Wilbur Dam (catalog watauga-river, batch-1 high-confidence record) - none of that record's facts are transferred here.

coldSource.notes: TWRA's Wilbur Tailwater Trout Fishery Management Plan 2022-2027 (cited URL, not fetched per PDF policy; text quoted in batch-1/wave-ledger records) fixes the geometry - Wilbur Dam at WRM 34 impounds a ~72-acre re-regulating pool about 3 miles below Watauga Dam - and documents turbine venting of Watauga Dam discharges so the chain's releases meet TVA's 6.0 mg/L DO target, i.e. deep (bottom) releases. Direct temperature evidence for water transiting this dam-to-dam chain: USGS-03483980 'WATAUGA RIVER AT WILBUR DAM, TN (TAILWATER)' - the discharge at the far (downstream) end of Wilbur Reservoir - measured 8.0 C (6/22/1976), 8.0 C (7/19/1976), 9.5 C (7/20/1976), 10.0 C (8/16/1976), 12.0-13.0 C in September, and 6.0-11.0 C across winter 1975-76 (WQP Result search below). Those samples sit below the 72-acre pool, so the release water is at or colder than that when it enters this reach; ~1,550 ft elevation per USGS 03484000 datum used for the chain in batch-1. Dam-release flow in this reach follows TVA generation schedules; minimum-flow/intermittency was not assessed in this pass.

holdover.detail: No fishery survey or holdover study specific to this 1.5-mile reach was found; TWRA's Wilbur plan documents holdover/survival for the tailwater BELOW Wilbur Dam (a different catalog entry), and the 2017-2027 statewide plan counts Wilbur Reservoir among the nine reservoirs with maintained trout fisheries. For the reach itself: unknown.

wildPopulation.detail: No natural-reproduction data specific to the reach. Trout stocked at both ends of the chain (Watauga Lake; Wilbur Reservoir Mar-Jul; Wilbur tailwater below) necessarily transit this water, but no in-reach survey documents reproduction.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: The release water transiting this Watauga-Dam-to-Wilbur chain measured 8.0-9.5 C in June-July 1976 and never exceeded 13 C in any season at the chain's discharge gauge (USGS-03483980) - bottom-draw dam water far below any summer trout stress threshold, year-round.

segment.description: West Fork Stones River, Rutherford County, Tennessee (catalog) — the named West Fork through Murfreesboro, anchored on USGS 03428200 'West Fork Stones River at Murfreesboro, TN'. TWRA's urban winter-trout site here is the Stones River Greenway at Manson Pike Trailhead. Identity disambiguation: this is the WEST Fork of the Stones (HUC 05130203) — not the Fort Campbell Little West Fork (batch-4 slug little-west-fork-creek, HUC 05130206), not the East Fork (east-fork-stones-river), and not the Davidson County mainstem (stones-river).
segment.boundaries: The named West Fork within Rutherford County; gauge 03428200 (35.90287, -86.42998; Rutherford Co.; 177 sq mi drainage; alt 514.31 ft NAVD88). The TWRA stocking site string is 'W. Fork Stones River - Manson Pike Trailhead' (workbook).

coldSource.notes: Elevation is the USGS gauge altitude at Murfreesboro (514.31 ft NAVD88, waterservices site output; identity verified via the waterservices site service because the USGS identity endpoint has been 503ing). NPS Water Resources Division station metadata for Stones River National Battlefield documents small spring inputs to the West Fork — Battlefield Spring ('discharging approximately 2 liters/minute into West Fork') and McFadden Spring (USGS 03428126, on the west bank ~300 ft downstream of Thompson Lane) — but these are trivially small discharges, not a reach-scale cold-water source. The same NPS station metadata records that 'West Fork Stones River itself is listed by the State of Tennessee as a 303d water.' TWRA's Percy Priest reservoir page documents the West Fork as a warmwater white bass/yellow bass spring-run fishery ('Productive fishing spots include the East and West Forks of the Stones River, as well as Stewart Creek') and contains no trout content. USGS has no instantaneous temperature sensor at 03428200 (IV query for July 2025 returned zero series).

holdover.detail: No holdover documentation found either way. The TWRA program at this site is a winter-only catchable-rainbow stocking (2026 workbook rows 'W. Fork Stones River - Manson Pike Trailhead': 02/04/2026, 2/27/2026, TBD 12/2026, Rainbow Trout, type Winter); agency text documents no between-stocking survival on this reach, and on-reach monitoring shows 28-30 deg C summer water (NPS grabs 2003-2024; USGS grab 30.0 deg C Aug 1988 at 03428200).

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documentation for the West Fork. TWRA's Trout Management Plan 2017-2027 places Tennessee's wild trout resources in East Tennessee streams and describes hatchery-supported waters as 'primarily warmwater habitats that cannot support trout year round' (plan PDF not fetched per no-PDF rule; URL cited). The urban greenway reach is a 303d-listed warmwater creek per NPS station metadata.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: On-reach agency monitoring records 28-30 deg C summer water at McFadden's Ford/Redoubt Brannon (2003-2024, NPS) and a 30.0 deg C USGS grab (1988), with the trout fishery being a winter-only catchable-rainbow program at Manson Pike Trailhead.
